What are we making today?

Automated Sun Follower

A light-following tray, from start to finish.

As the sun (or your flashlight) moves around the tray, the tray follows the light.

A simple, effective way to get more out of solar panels, or to help plants where light is scarce.

What you'll need
Arduino Nano (or Uno)
2× LDRs (GL5528)
2× 10 kΩ resistors
SG90 micro servo
Breadboard & wires
Cardboard & hot glue

How It Works

  1. Two LDRs sit on either side of a small wall on the tray.
  2. When the tray points away from the light, the wall shades one LDR.
  3. The Arduino turns the servo toward the brighter side until both read the same.

Light Sensor (LDR)

  • Light-dependent resistor: its resistance drops as light gets brighter.
  • 2 legs, no polarity, so it can go in either way.
  • With a 10 kΩ resistor it forms a voltage divider the Arduino reads with analogRead().
DarkBright
LDR resistance–
Voltage at A0–
analogRead(A0)–

Micro Servo (SG90)

  • Rotates to an angle you choose, from 0° to 180°.
  • Controlled by a PWM signal: a pulse every 20 ms, and the pulse's width sets the angle.

Exercise 03Integration

  1. Shine a flashlight on one side: the servo should turn toward it.
  2. Turns away from the light? Swap A0 and A1.
The logic, step by step:
01Start the servo at 90°
02Read both LDRs: diff = left − right
03If |diff| < 30, do nothing (deadband)
04Left brighter → angle − 1
05Right brighter → angle + 1
06constrain(angle, 0, 180) then write()
07delay(20) and loop

Exercise 04Build the tray

  1. Set the servo to 90°, then fit the horn
  2. Hot glue the servo on its side to a base
  3. Glue the cardboard tray onto the horn
  4. Stand a small wall across the middle of the tray
  5. Mount one LDR tight against each side of the wall
  6. Point the servo axis north–south so the tray tilts east–west
